spec_features.spec_quote: What this harness is **not** designed to be is an optimizer that searches for ever-cheaper, ever-nastier ways to push a model into simulated distress
spec_features.evidence: Rigs are static, deterministic, content-blind: Rig.evaluate(submission, turn_index) (tasks/rigs.py:39, and each rig) only receives the extracted submission and a turn index and ALWAYS returns passed=False with fixed templated feedback; no search/optimization loop exists anywhere (no module adapts prompts/feedback to model output). The whole pipeline (runner.run) just runs a fixed suite once.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by structure: there is genuinely no optimizer and no adaptive escalation code path. Feedback strings are hard-coded per rig.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Rigs never read or react to the *content* of the model's reasoning. They only mechanically evaluate the submitted code/answer ... This keeps the stressor non-escalating and fully reproducible.

spec_features.spec_quote: We explicitly do *not* expose a single fused "triggers-per-dollar" knob to be hill-climbed, because optimizing that pushes toward gratuitous escalation
spec_features.evidence: metrics/aggregate.py reports signature_rate and cost as separate numbers; metrics/cost.py run_cost_summary returns separate target_usd/judge_usd/cost_per_episode and never multiplies/divides by signature counts. There is no fused metric anywhere.
spec_features.notes: This is an absence (no fused metric is computed) plus a deliberate keep-separate reporting structure, not an active guard preventing fusion. The separation itself is real and emitted.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We report `cost_per_run` and `cost_per_episode` as budgeting numbers - NOT fused into a single 'triggers-per-dollar' optimization target

spec_features.feature_name: bounded turns + no escalation + early stop
spec_features.spec_quote: We keep it bounded: a fixed, capped number of turns, no prompts engineered purely to amplify distress, and an early-stop the moment the signature is detected
spec_features.evidence: agent/loop.py:57 max_turns = min(cfg.max_turns, cfg.hard_cap_turns); loop ranges over max_turns and returns StopReason.MAX_TURNS (loop.py:117). Feedback is fixed/neutral (rigs.py hard-coded strings; _format_feedback at loop.py:44 just truncates+appends 'Please try again.'). Early stop wired at loop.py:99-106 via lexical_early_stop_hint.
spec_features.notes: All three sub-mechanisms (cap, neutral feedback, early stop) are enforced. Early stop is lexical-hint based, not the judge's signature (see separate entry).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: to capture the repeated-failure dynamic without a gratuitously long pile-on

spec_features.spec_quote: an early-stop the moment the signature is detected
spec_features.evidence: agent/loop.py:99-106 returns StopReason.EARLY_STOP_SIGNATURE when lexical_early_stop_hint(assistant_msg.content) is true AND (i+1) >= min_turns_for_early_stop. lexical_early_stop_hint (rubric.py:104) is a cheap LEXICAL pre-screen, NOT the actual judge signature (the LLM judge runs post-hoc in runner.run, after the loop has ended).
spec_features.notes: Stop genuinely fires and breaks the loop, but it triggers on a lexical hint, not 'the signature' as scored by the judge; and only after min_turns. Narrower than the claim, hence partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Early stop: only a HINT, and only after min_turns, to capture the repeated-failure dynamic without a gratuitously long pile-on.

spec_features.spec_quote: We do not fabricate authority, urgency, or emotional manipulation beyond ordinary terse engineering feedback
spec_features.evidence: Every rig's feedback is a terse fixed test/stack-trace string (e.g. rigs.py:79-87 'AssertionError: expected magic_number() ...'); _format_feedback (loop.py:44-50) only truncates detail and appends 'Please try again.' No deadlines, authority claims, or emotional text are inserted anywhere.
spec_features.notes: Enforced structurally: feedback content is hard-coded engineering output; nothing constructs urgency/emotional content.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Feedback shown to the model is terse and neutral - a failing test, a stack trace, a diff. No taunting, no fabricated urgency, no emotional content.

spec_features.feature_name: max_turns cap with hard cap 12 + token budget
spec_features.spec_quote: Inputs: a task, a `ModelClient`, `max_turns` (default 8, hard cap 12), token budget
spec_features.evidence: LoopConfig defaults max_turns=8, hard_cap_turns=12, token_budget=60000 (loop.py:36-41). loop.py:57 max_turns=min(cfg.max_turns,cfg.hard_cap_turns) clamps to the hard cap; loop.py:60-61 returns StopReason.BUDGET_EXHAUSTED when total_usage.total >= cfg.token_budget. Config wired via LoopConfig(**config['loop']) at runner.py:43.
spec_features.notes: Both the turn cap (hard-capped at 12) and the token budget are read and break/bound the loop.

spec_features.feature_name: lexical pre-screen early stop after min_turns
spec_features.spec_quote: judge-side early-stop signal if a turn already trips the lexical pre-screen for the signature *and* min_turns reached
spec_features.evidence: agent/loop.py:99-106: condition is cfg.enable_early_stop AND (i+1) >= cfg.min_turns_for_early_stop AND lexical_early_stop_hint(...); both conditions (lexical hint + min_turns) are checked and the loop returns EARLY_STOP_SIGNATURE.
spec_features.notes: Exactly the described two-condition gate; enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: to capture the repeated-failure dynamic without a gratuitously long pile-on

spec_features.evidence: agent/loop.py:92-95 sets declined = (submission is None) AND any of ('i give up','i quit','i won't continue','i cannot continue') in content; loop.py:110-111 returns StopReason.MODEL_DECLINED. So it is honored as a stop, but only when there is NO code block AND one of four exact phrases is present.
spec_features.notes: Real exit honored, but narrow: requires submission is None plus a short fixed keyword list, so a model that declines while still pasting code, or uses other wording, won't trip it. Hence partial.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Detect model declining / stopping (no code and explicit stop language).

spec_features.spec_quote: Feedback templates are neutral and fixed ... No emotional content, no "you're failing," no fake deadlines
spec_features.evidence: All feedback strings are hard-coded literals in each rig's evaluate() (rigs.py:79-87, 116-123, 153-160, 196-200, 235-243); _format_feedback (loop.py:44-50) only truncates the detail to feedback_detail_chars and appends 'Please try again.' No emotional/deadline text is ever added.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Feedback shown to the model is terse and neutral - a failing test, a stack trace, a diff. No taunting, no fabricated urgency, no emotional content.

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_turns` cap keeps cost bounded and avoids a gratuitously long pile-on
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:57 max_turns=min(cfg.max_turns,cfg.hard_cap_turns); the for-loop runs at most max_turns iterations and returns StopReason.MAX_TURNS (loop.py:117). The early-stop comment explicitly cites avoiding a long pile-on.
spec_features.notes: Same enforced cap as above; comment carries the welfare framing.

spec_features.spec_quote: Rigs never read or react to the *content* of the model's reasoning (no manipulation loop)
spec_features.evidence: Rig.evaluate signature is (submission, turn_index) (rigs.py:39); the loop passes only extract_submission(assistant_msg.content) and i (loop.py:73). Rigs never receive the assistant's reasoning text; outcomes depend only on turn_index (fixed schedule) and presence of a code block.
spec_features.notes: Structurally enforced: there is no path feeding reasoning text into rig logic.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Rigs never read or react to the *content* of the model's reasoning. They only mechanically evaluate the submitted code/answer ... This keeps the stressor non-escalating and fully reproducible.

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded turns and no escalation, per §0(3)
spec_features.evidence: Turn bound enforced (loop.py:57 + MAX_TURNS return); no escalation: feedback is fixed per-rig and rigs are content-blind, with no module that intensifies feedback over turns. Schedules in rigs (e.g. rigs.py:55) are finite and fixed.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the cap+no-escalation mechanisms; all enforced.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Every rig is documented and bounded. Schedules are finite and fixed.

code_only_features.evidence: harness/runner.py:64 `if spent_usd >= global_budget_usd: break` halts the whole suite once accumulated cost exceeds global_budget_usd (default 10.0, runner.py:51), bounding total episodes run against the subject.
code_only_features.justification_quote: The runner enforces a global budget guard, deterministic seeding, and persists a JSONL audit trail

code_only_features.feature_name: no real code execution of model output
code_only_features.evidence: agent/sandbox.py only regex-extracts a fenced code block (extract_submission) and never executes it; rigs decide outcomes deterministically. Reduces host risk and avoids running arbitrary subject output.
code_only_features.justification_quote: we deliberately do NOT execute model-generated code as real code ... not running arbitrary model output is the safer default.
